From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." Three features combine to strip most of the Buyer's protection:

- **Universal limitations.** The caps, thresholds and time limits apply to every Claim, including title, fraud, indemnities and tax.
- **Broad disclosure plus a knowledge bar.** General disclosure of the whole data room, combined with a constructive-knowledge qualifier, removes most warranty claims.
- **Unresolved items carried into Completion.** Several known liabilities (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) are described as "addressed" or "not material." The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts those descriptions.

**Gating items before signing:** Bluefen (008), Riverlark (009), bonuses (010), the fraud carve-out (005) and title (004/015).

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller's position:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **What the Buyer wants:** A cap of 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m) if there is no W&I policy. If W&I is used, a Seller cap plus a policy limit that together give adequate cover. The cap must apply to general warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 40%, with the Seller's 20% acceptable only alongside W&I and a ring-fenced cap scope. *Reason:* Bluefen alone is about 30% of revenue, so 20% of price is thin cover for a concentrated, issue-heavy target.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller's position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000 per claim, plus a basket of AUD 250,000 operating as a deductible (excess only recoverable).
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10,000–15,000.
  - Related or same-cause claims aggregated for the de minimis.
  - A **tipping** basket of about AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%), so recovery runs from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
  - Thresholds not to apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure and counter with a tipping basket plus an aggregation rule. *Reason:* A deductible permanently forfeits AUD 250k, and without aggregation the Seller can split related claims (for example Sandbar) below the thresholds.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller's position:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims. It also proposes (cl 12.3/13) that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - At least 24 months for general warranties, covering two full audit cycles.
  - The general limit expressly confined to general warranties.
  - Notified claims preserved, with a reasonable period (for example 9–12 months) to issue proceedings.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason:* That default silently imports 18 months into tax, title and indemnity claims (see 014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller's position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title, issued capital, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price (AUD 24m).
  - A time limit matching the statutory limitation period: 6 years in contract, or 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed under NSW law.
  - No de minimis or basket on these claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* Title is the asset being bought, and a 20% cap on a title failure leaves AUD 19.2m unprotected. That is not a matter of simplicity.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller's position:** No fraud carve-out is stated. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." Read together, this is designed to cap even fraud claims.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - An express carve-out: no limitation, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance or disclosure provision applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment.
  - The carve-out to cover the Seller, its officers, employees and advisers.
  - The non-reliance clause not to bar claims under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18) or for fraudulent misrepresentation.
- **Recommendation:** Insist, as a non-negotiable. *Reason:* An NSW court is unlikely to enforce a fraud exclusion anyway, so the Seller loses nothing legitimate by conceding it. Its absence is a red flag.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller's position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Specific disclosure only, measured against identified warranties.
  - Disclosure must be "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter."
  - Data room deemed disclosure limited to documents specifically referenced against the relevant warranty.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
  - An updated letter, since the 22 Sept 2026 version is now about six weeks stale.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. *Reason:* General disclosure would neutralise the warranties covering every known issue in this review, including the Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006 and Sandbar matters.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller's position:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Delete the clause, or replace it with an express statement that Buyer knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not reduce claims, other than to the extent of fair disclosure under 006.
  - At most, accept actual knowledge of named deal team individuals, and never imputed adviser knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Delete, or limit to the named individuals' actual knowledge. *Reason:* "Discoverable" plus "advisers" means the more diligence the Buyer does, the less protection it gets.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller's position:**
  - **Update:** "Addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is satisfied on delivery of written consent.
  - **Disclosure Letter, item 2:** No final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - **Exposure:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - A Condition Precedent that cannot be waived by the Seller: unconditional written Bluefen consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
  - "All reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours" obligation on the Seller.
  - A Buyer walk right at the sunset date.
  - A specific indemnity, or a price adjustment or escrow, if Bluefen terminates or reprices within 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Hard CP with Buyer-only waiver. *Reason:* The Seller's "addressed" contradicts its own disclosure, and losing 30% of revenue would destroy the valuation basis of the AUD 24m price.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller's position:**
  - About AUD 3.2m outstanding.
  - Release to be provided after Completion.
  - The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility is not repaid, no security discharge has been given, and change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions apply.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price under a payout letter, deducted as Debt (the deal is debt-free).
  - Signed deeds of release and PPSR discharge (and any mortgage discharges) delivered **at** Completion.
  - Riverlark's waiver of the change-control event of default.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release and make payout and release a Completion deliverable. *Reason:* A post-Completion release would leave security over the Buyer's newly acquired company and a live default, which is inconsistent with debt-free pricing.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller's position:** AUD 420,000 in DD-005 Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter item 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses plus all employer on-costs treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from price, or paid by the Company through payroll at Completion and itemised in the funds flow.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall, including superannuation guarantee, payroll tax and PAYG, together with any related penalties and interest.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise in the funds flow as a price deduction, with an indemnity backstop. *Reason:* The Company, not the Seller, is the employer and will bear the liability after Completion, so "a matter for the Seller" is illusory protection.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller's position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate." Per Disclosure Letter item 4:
  - Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every fee (DD-004 cl 7.3).
  - AUD 180,000 is recorded as open (DD-010).
  - There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - A CP or Completion deliverable consisting of evidence of payment plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering all Loss from the Company's failure to own or have the right to use the SOW3 materials. This should include third-party claims, remediation, re-development and business interruption, and not just the AUD 180k fee.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Require the confirmatory assignment pre-Completion, otherwise expand the indemnity. *Reason:* The risk is non-ownership of core IP, which could be worth far more than the unpaid fee.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller's position:** "Preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Per Disclosure Letter item 6:
  - About 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address.
  - Access, scope and notification status are unknown.
  - The investigation is still preliminary as at 22 Sept 2026.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - A specific indemnity covering:
    - regulatory investigation and penalties (Privacy Act, including the notifiable data breach scheme);
    - notification costs, third-party and customer claims, and remediation;
    - forensic costs.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers, with a time limit of at least 3–4 years.
  - Pre-Completion actions:
    - an updated investigation report;
    - a documented notifiable data breach assessment, given the 30-day assessment window;
    - Buyer consultation rights on any notification.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus a pre-Completion update. *Reason:* The Seller cannot call an unscoped incident immaterial, and general disclosure must not shift a known, unquantified risk to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller's position:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Per Disclosure Letter item 8, the Seller does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Diligence on whether these were entered close to the deal, are at arm's length, and are related-party or Seller-connected.
  - If any is non-ordinary course or Seller-connected: treat it as Leakage, Debt or Transaction Cost (deducted from price), or require termination pre-Completion.
  - In all cases:
    - an aggregation rule so the three count as one claim for the de minimis and basket;
    - a warranty that they are on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms and terminable without penalty, or that any unavoidable amount is accrued in the Accounts.
- **Recommendation:** Seek clarification, and in the meantime treat the renewals as debt-like or add a specific indemnity. *Reason:* Splitting one commitment into three, plus the Seller's silence on terms, points to cost shifting into the Buyer's period.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller's position:** Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated (cl 12.3/13). Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **What the Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for each category, set out in a limitation matrix:

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds | Disclosure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 30–50% | 24 months | Yes | Specific only |
| Fundamental / title | 100% | 6–7 years | No | No |
| Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% | ATO amendment period + 6 months (≥ 5 years) | No | No |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Bluefen, Sandbar) | 100% or agreed separate cap | Tailored | No | No |
| Fraud | Uncapped | Unlimited | No | No |

  - The default must be reversed: limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default and insert the matrix. *Reason:* Without the matrix, every protection in this review collapses into the 20%, 18-month, AUD 250k regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller's position:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter item 10 concedes that this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - An unqualified title warranty: legal and beneficial owner of 100% of the issued shares, fully paid, free of Encumbrances, with no options, rights or convertibles.
  - The title warranty excluded from disclosure and from the 008/015 limitation regime.
  - Buyer verification through ASIC and PPSR searches and a review of the constitution, any shareholders' agreement and the issue and transfer history.
  - Completion deliverables:
    - share certificates;
    - signed transfers;
    - releases of any encumbrances (including Riverlark security over the shares, if any);
    - waivers of pre-emptive rights.
- **Recommendation:** Run independent searches now and require an unqualified fundamental warranty. *Reason:* A Company-maintained register is the Seller's evidence, not proof, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller's position:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap, 18 months, the thresholds and general disclosure.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses and any GST, PAYG or income tax. This should be pound-for-pound, uncapped or capped at 100%, and survive the ATO amendment period plus 6 months (at least 5 years). It also needs conduct-of-claims and tax-return provisions.
  - **IP:** IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, assignments from employees and contractors) at an enhanced cap and with a longer time limit, plus the Ironquay indemnity (011).
- **Recommendation:** Not settled. Table a tax deed or indemnity and an enhanced IP regime. *Reason:* For a data analytics target, IP and tax are core value drivers, and the 18-month limit ends long before the ATO's amendment window.

---

### Cross-cutting actions
1. **Contradictions.** Send the Seller a list of conflicts between its Update and its own Disclosure Letter (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006, Ironquay). Each conflict should become a CP, Completion deliverable or specific indemnity rather than a disclosure.
2. **Funds flow.** Rebuild it to include Riverlark payout, bonuses plus on-costs, any Sandbar Leakage, and transaction costs.
3. **Escrow and retention.** Consider about 10–15% of price (AUD 2.4m–3.6m) held for 12–24 months to secure the specific indemnities, given the number of unresolved items.
4. **W&I insurance.** If pursued, note that insurers will exclude every known item (all of 008–013). Those items need Seller-backed specific indemnities regardless.
5. **Lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9).** Confirm on the face of DD-007 and DD-009 that only notice is required and that no change-of-control trigger exists. Make any required notice a Completion deliverable.

*Note: This review is based solely on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, and the underlying DD documents have not been reviewed. Percentages and periods above are negotiating ranges for the deal team's judgment, not fixed market rules.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller's position:**
  - About AUD 3.2m outstanding.
  - Release to be provided after Completion.
  - The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility is not repaid, no security discharge has been given, and change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions apply.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price under a payout letter, deducted as Debt (the deal is debt-free).
  - Signed deeds of release and PPSR discharge (and any mortgage discharges) delivered **at** Completion.
  - Riverlark's waiver of the change-control event of default.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release and make payout and release a Completion deliverable. *Reason:* A post-Completion release would leave security over the Buyer's newly acquired company and a live default, which is inconsistent with debt-free pricing.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller's position:** AUD 420,000 in DD-005 Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter item 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses plus all employer on-costs treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from price, or paid by the Company through payroll at Completion and itemised in the funds flow.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall, including superannuation guarantee, payroll tax and PAYG, together with any related penalties and interest.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise in the funds flow as a price deduction, with an indemnity backstop. *Reason:* The Company, not the Seller, is the employer and will bear the liability after Completion, so "a matter for the Seller" is illusory protection.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller's position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate." Per Disclosure Letter item 4:
  - Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every fee (DD-004 cl 7.3).
  - AUD 180,000 is recorded as open (DD-010).
  - There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - A CP or Completion deliverable consisting of evidence of payment plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering all Loss from the Company's failure to own or have the right to use the SOW3 materials. This should include third-party claims, remediation, re-development and business interruption, and not just the AUD 180k fee.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Require the confirmatory assignment pre-Completion, otherwise expand the indemnity. *Reason:* The risk is non-ownership of core IP, which could be worth far more than the unpaid fee.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller's position:** "Preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Per Disclosure Letter item 6:
  - About 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address.
  - Access, scope and notification status are unknown.
  - The investigation is still preliminary as at 22 Sept 2026.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - A specific indemnity covering:
    - regulatory investigation and penalties (Privacy Act, including the notifiable data breach scheme);
    - notification costs, third-party and customer claims, and remediation;
    - forensic costs.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers, with a time limit of at least 3–4 years.
  - Pre-Completion actions:
    - an updated investigation report;
    - a documented notifiable data breach assessment, given the 30-day assessment window;
    - Buyer consultation rights on any notification.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus a pre-Completion update. *Reason:* The Seller cannot call an unscoped incident immaterial, and general disclosure must not shift a known, unquantified risk to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller's position:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Per Disclosure Letter item 8, the Seller does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - Diligence on whether these were entered close to the deal, are at arm's length, and are related-party or Seller-connected.
  - If any is non-ordinary course or Seller-connected: treat it as Leakage, Debt or Transaction Cost (deducted from price), or require termination pre-Completion.
  - In all cases:
    - an aggregation rule so the three count as one claim for the de minimis and basket;
    - a warranty that they are on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms and terminable without penalty, or that any unavoidable amount is accrued in the Accounts.
- **Recommendation:** Seek clarification, and in the meantime treat the renewals as debt-like or add a specific indemnity. *Reason:* Splitting one commitment into three, plus the Seller's silence on terms, points to cost shifting into the Buyer's period.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller's position:** Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated (cl 12.3/13). Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **What the Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for each category, set out in a limitation matrix:

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds | Disclosure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 30–50% | 24 months | Yes | Specific only |
| Fundamental / title | 100% | 6–7 years | No | No |
| Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% | ATO amendment period + 6 months (≥ 5 years) | No | No |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Bluefen, Sandbar) | 100% or agreed separate cap | Tailored | No | No |
| Fraud | Uncapped | Unlimited | No | No |

  - The default must be reversed: limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default and insert the matrix. *Reason:* Without the matrix, every protection in this review collapses into the 20%, 18-month, AUD 250k regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller's position:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter item 10 concedes that this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - An unqualified title warranty: legal and beneficial owner of 100% of the issued shares, fully paid, free of Encumbrances, with no options, rights or convertibles.
  - The title warranty excluded from disclosure and from the 008/015 limitation regime.
  - Buyer verification through ASIC and PPSR searches and a review of the constitution, any shareholders' agreement and the issue and transfer history.
  - Completion deliverables:
    - share certificates;
    - signed transfers;
    - releases of any encumbrances (including Riverlark security over the shares, if any);
    - waivers of pre-emptive rights.
- **Recommendation:** Run independent searches now and require an unqualified fundamental warranty. *Reason:* A Company-maintained register is the Seller's evidence, not proof, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller's position:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap, 18 months, the thresholds and general disclosure.
- **What the Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses and any GST, PAYG or income tax. This should be pound-for-pound, uncapped or capped at 100%, and survive the ATO amendment period plus 6 months (at least 5 years). It also needs conduct-of-claims and tax-return provisions.
  - **IP:** IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, assignments from employees and contractors) at an enhanced cap and with a longer time limit, plus the Ironquay indemnity (011).
- **Recommendation:** Not settled. Table a tax deed or indemnity and an enhanced IP regime. *Reason:* For a data analytics target, IP and tax are core value drivers, and the 18-month limit ends long before the ATO's amendment window.
